decision.summaryForCoordinator: FC-SCHEMA is the class where the sha256 prohibition has real surface, because its exactByteIntent says in terms 'Each golden is pinned by sha256'. That is settled by counting, not by reading negations: the subject contains exactly seven DISTINCT 64-hex strings and exactly seven TOTAL occurrences, and all seven are cited-artifact digests — there is no eighth and no repeat, so no hex is available to be doing duty as a golden pin, and all twenty sha256 fields carry the bare token NOT-AUTHORED. The highest-risk invention vector was different and I tested it hardest: the five outcomeClassName values appear nowhere in the quoted exactByteIntent, so every one is an assertion beyond the quotation. All five (id, name) pairs were compared as an ordered list against live v4's outcomeStructure and are EXACTLY EQUAL — allChecksSatisfied, environmentDefectFound, reportIncomplete, invocationRefused, doctorFault. The inventory itself was rebuilt from four independent live enumerations rather than read: v4's modes.principle fixes the count at 'Exactly two modes exist. No third mode', the outcome classes number five, the status tokens are a closed set of five equal to the subject's list in order, and the enumerated degraded cases are DEG-1..DEG-7. Two plus five plus five plus seven is nineteen, and a Counter over namedGoldens returns exactly nineteen partitioned 2/5/5/7 with no duplicate id. Both boundary attacks fail: the subject correctly excludes v4's two absorbed degraded cases, which expressly have no separate entry and whose inclusion would have invented two goldens, and it correctly adds no golden per check class, a tempting fifth limb the pin does not name. Its handling of 'one per mode' is a genuine strength rather than a defect avoided by luck — it states outright that this means the two schema modes and not a re-authoring of FC-MODE's four invocations, which is right against both live sources. exactByteIntent is character-for-character equal to live v4 and the reader quotation is a true substring. Twenty attacks run, twenty refuted, zero findings. One thing needs your judgement rather than mine. I pressed the G12 annotation as a SHOULD-FIX and it did not cross, but it is sharper here than in the two preceding reviews: 'the last Claude ACCEPT 0/0 G12 subject' was already false when these bytes landed, by 10.399 seconds, where in FC-RO and FC-NC it was true at authoring and only overtaken afterwards.
